label: Homeowners (HO-3, standard)
wind: Usually covered as a named peril, but Florida and other coastal states often carry a separate hurricane deductible (a percentage of your home's value, not a flat dollar amount) that applies once a hurricane watch/warning is issued.
flood: Not covered. Standard homeowners policies exclude flood and storm surge entirely, no matter the cause.
action: Check your declarations page for a separate hurricane/windstorm deductible, and get a flood policy (NFIP or private) if you don't have one - it's not automatic.

label: Renters (HO-4)
wind: Your belongings are usually covered if wind-driven rain gets in through storm damage (like a broken window), but the building itself is your landlord's responsibility, not yours.
flood: Not covered. Renters policies exclude flood damage to your belongings just like homeowners policies do.
action: A separate flood policy through NFIP or a private insurer can cover your belongings even as a renter - most people don't know this exists.

label: Condo (HO-6)
wind: Your unit's interior and belongings are usually covered; the building structure is typically the condo association's master policy - check what "walls in" vs "walls out" means for your specific association.
flood: Not covered by either your HO-6 policy or most master policies. Flood needs a separate policy, and it's worth asking your HOA if the building itself carries one.
action: Ask your condo association exactly what their master policy covers, and get your own flood policy for your unit's contents.

label: Mobile / manufactured home
wind: Often more restrictive than standard homeowners coverage - many insurers require the home to be properly anchored/tied down to code, and some carriers won't write wind coverage at all in high-risk areas.
flood: Not covered, same as any other policy type - and mobile homes are not safe to shelter in during a hurricane regardless of insurance.
action: Confirm your home meets current anchoring requirements, and evacuate whenever a hurricane threatens - insurance doesn't change that guidance.
source: Insurance Information Institute (iii.org); National Weather Service

label: Auto - liability only
wind: Not covered. Liability insurance only pays for damage or injuries you cause to OTHER people or property - it never pays to repair your own car, no matter the cause.
flood: Not covered, for the same reason - liability-only never touches your own vehicle.
action: Add comprehensive coverage if you want storm damage to your own car covered - liability alone leaves you fully exposed.

label: Auto - full coverage (comprehensive)
wind: Covered. Comprehensive coverage ("other than collision") pays for wind, hail, and falling-object damage to your own car.
flood: Covered. Comprehensive also covers flood and storm surge damage to your own vehicle.
action: You're covered for storm damage - just document everything with photos before repairs, and check if you have rental reimbursement if your car needs time in the shop.

label: Flood policy (NFIP or private)
wind: Not covered by a flood policy specifically - wind damage is handled by your homeowners/renters/condo policy instead.
flood: Covered, for the structure and/or contents depending on what you purchased - check which one(s) you bought.
action: NFIP policies take about 30 days to take effect, so buying one right before a storm won't help for that storm - get it before hurricane season starts.

label: Not sure / other policy type
wind: We don't have a confident, sourced answer for this without knowing your actual policy type and state - coverage varies too much to guess.
flood: Same here - we can't tell you this without knowing your specific policy.
action: Check your policy's declarations page for the named perils it lists, or call your agent and ask directly: "Does this cover wind damage? Does it cover flood or storm surge?" That's the only reliable way to know for your exact policy.
source: N/A - insufficient information to give a sourced answer
